classes.objetivo: Distinguir obligación, prohibición, permiso y ausencia de obligación en normas escolares y vecinales (must, have to, be required to, must not, be permitted to, don't have to) y reconocer el marcador de cada una.

ensenanza.en: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.
ensenanza.es: Según el reglamento del colegio, todos los alumnos deben llevar el uniforme y cumplir con el código de vestimenta en todas las clases.
ensenanza.nota: Be required to + verbo: obligación formal; el reglamento no dice «debes», sino «se exige». Comply with + norma: cumplirla.

ensenanza.en: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.
ensenanza.es: La asistencia a la asamblea de la mañana es obligatoria, mientras que unirse al coro es totalmente opcional, así que nadie puede ser obligado a cantar.
ensenanza.nota: Compulsory (y mandatory) son adjetivos de obligación propios de los reglamentos; optional marca lo que cada uno decide.

ensenanza.en: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are permitted to use them at break in the yard.
ensenanza.es: Los teléfonos móviles están estrictamente prohibidos durante las clases, aunque los alumnos tienen permiso para usarlos en el recreo en el patio.
ensenanza.nota: Are prohibited: prohibición formal, equivale a must not. Are permitted to + verbo: permiso formal, equivale a may o are allowed to.

ensenanza.en: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.
ensenanza.es: Los alumnos de bachillerato estarán exentos de la norma del uniforme, así que no tienen que llevarlo, pero llevarlo tampoco está prohibido.
ensenanza.nota: Be exempt from + norma: quedar libre de una obligación. No tener que hacer algo (don't have to) no equivale a tenerlo prohibido (forbidden).

ensenanza.en: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.
ensenanza.es: El personal no debe aparcar frente a la puerta, porque la obligación de mantener despejada la entrada se aplica a todos sin excepción.
ensenanza.nota: Must not = prohibido. Ojo: no equivale a don't have to, que solo dice «no hace falta». Obligation es el sustantivo de lo que se debe hacer.

ensenanza.en: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations leave the choice of project topic to each student.
ensenanza.es: Aunque el examen final es obligatorio para todos, el reglamento deja a cada alumno la elección del tema del proyecto.
ensenanza.nota: Mandatory = obligatorio, sin excepción. Although + oración: contraste, no lleva but en la misma frase.

explicacion.texto: En un reglamento, la fuerza de la norma depende de la expresión. Obligación: must, have to, are required to, is compulsory. Prohibición: must not, may not, are not permitted to, is prohibited. Permiso: may, can, are allowed to, are permitted to. Y una trampa: don't have to significa que no es necesario (es opcional), no que esté prohibido; para prohibir se usa must not. El español mezcla «no debes» y «no tienes que», y de ahí la confusión.

patron.texto: Sujeto + be required / permitted + to + verbo base:

formula.nota: fuerza: obligación (o are permitted to = permiso)
verbo base + lo que se exige

filas.texto: must · have to · are required to · is compulsory
must not · may not · are not permitted to · is prohibited
may · can · are allowed to · are permitted to
don't have to · need not · is optional

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: You mustn't wear the uniform on Fridays; it is optional.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: You don't have to wear the uniform on Fridays.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Mustn't prohíbe; para decir que no es necesario se usa don't have to.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Students are prohibited to use phones in class.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Students are not permitted to use phones in class.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Prohibited va con from + -ing; con to + verbo se dice not permitted to.

situacion.contexto: Mia es nueva en el colegio y Leo le explica el reglamento el primer día.

dialogo.texto: Do I have to wear a tie?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Tengo que llevar corbata?

dialogo.texto: No, it is optional. But the uniform is compulsory.
dialogo.traduccion: No, es opcional. Pero el uniforme es obligatorio.

dialogo.texto: Can I use my phone at break?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Puedo usar el móvil en el recreo?

dialogo.texto: Yes, phones are permitted at break, but they are prohibited in class.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí, los móviles están permitidos en el recreo, pero prohibidos en clase.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué reglas explica Leo?

opciones.es: La corbata es opcional, el uniforme es obligatorio y el móvil solo se permite en el recreo.
La corbata es obligatoria y el móvil está prohibido siempre.
El uniforme es opcional y el móvil se permite en clase.

item.feedback: Leo dice que la corbata es «optional», el uniforme «compulsory» y que los móviles están permitidos en el recreo pero prohibidos en clase.

opciones: Riding a bicycle in the playground.
Locking a bicycle at the gate.
Cycling to school in the morning.
guiada.feedback: Are prohibited expresa una prohibición formal; permitted da permiso y optional deja la decisión libre.
guiada.texto: School notice: bicycles are prohibited in the playground, but pupils are permitted to lock them at the gate. Nobody is forced to cycle to school, because it is optional.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «La asistencia a la asamblea es obligatoria para todo el colegio.»
guiada.texto: Every pupil has to be in the hall at nine. Attendance at the assembly is ___ for the whole school, and nobody can be excused without a note.
guiada.feedback: Compulsory (o mandatory) califica una obligación que no admite excepción.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo de obligación que aparece en los reglamentos.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Los visitantes no tienen permiso para entrar en la cocina.»
guiada.respuesta: Visitors are not permitted to enter the kitchen
guiada.feedback: Are not permitted to + verbo base es una prohibición formal; la negación va tras are.
guiada.pista: Empieza con Visitors; la negación va justo después de are.

practica.consigna: Escucha a la directora y elige qué es obligatorio para los alumnos.
practica.audio: At the start of term, the head teacher read out the regulations. Every student is required to wear the uniform, she said, and arriving on time is compulsory: anyone who comes late must sign in at the office. Mobile phones are prohibited in class, although students are permitted to use them during break. Wearing a tie is optional, so nobody has to buy one, but running in the corridors is forbidden, for safety. She added that staff would comply with the same rules whenever they walked through the school with pupils.
opciones: Signing in at the office when they arrive late.
Wearing a tie to every lesson of the school day.
Keeping their phones switched off for the whole break.
practica.feedback: Quien llega tarde debe firmar en la oficina: es obligatorio. La corbata es opcional y los móviles están permitidos en el recreo.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la fuerza de la norma.
pares: All pupils are required to wear a badge.
Bags are forbidden in the laboratory.
You may leave early on Fridays.
Year eleven will be exempt from assembly.
practica.feedback: Required marca obligación, forbidden prohibición, may permiso y be exempt from una liberación de la obligación.

practica.consigna: Lee el boletín: ¿qué postura refleja sobre la corbata?
opciones: It accepts a small change while keeping the main rule.
It drops the uniform rule completely.
It makes the tie stricter than before.
practica.feedback: La corbata pasa a ser opcional, pero el uniforme sigue siendo obligatorio: un cambio pequeño que mantiene la norma principal.
practica.texto: Dear parents, from September the uniform will remain compulsory, but the tie becomes optional. The school believes the change will reduce costs without lowering standards. Staff will check the uniform during the first week, and any student who is not in full uniform will be asked to comply by the next day.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la reunión y elige qué es obligatorio para los dueños de perros.
evaluacion.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.
opciones: Keeping the dog on a lead in the park.
Walking the dog on the grass near the playground.
Leaving the dog at home on weekend mornings.
evaluacion.feedback: Mandatory marca la obligación: el perro va con correa en el resto del parque. Pasear por la hierba es un permiso.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha otra vez: ¿con qué fin menciona el presidente la multa?
evaluacion.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.
opciones: To show that the lead rule will be taken seriously.
To announce a new fine for cyclists on the pavement.
To ask owners to pay for damage.
evaluacion.feedback: La multa se menciona como consecuencia de no cumplir la norma de la correa: subraya que se aplicará en serio.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Todo el personal debe cumplir con el nuevo reglamento.»
evaluacion.texto: The new regulations apply from Monday. All staff are required to ___ with them, or they may be fined.
evaluacion.feedback: Comply with + norma significa cumplirla; se construye con with.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Es obligatorio llevar el uniforme en todas las clases.»
evaluacion.respuesta: Wearing the uniform is mandatory in every lesson
evaluacion.feedback: Mandatory es el adjetivo de obligación sin excepción; wearing el uniforme funciona como sujeto de la frase.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué quiere dejar claro la profesora sobre la norma de la piscina?
repaso.audio: A sign at the pool says that children under ten may not swim without an adult, and a teacher explained the rule to a group of pupils. The aim is not to spoil anyone's fun, she said, but to keep the younger children safe. Older pupils are permitted to swim alone, provided that a lifeguard is here, and nobody is required to join the lesson if they have a note from home.
opciones: That the rule exists to protect young children, not to blame anyone.
That older pupils must swim with an adult.
That the lesson is compulsory for everybody.
repaso.feedback: Dice que el objetivo no es estropear la diversión sino proteger a los más pequeños: la norma protege, no culpa a nadie.

repaso.consigna: Lee el aviso: ¿qué se puede deducir?
opciones: A jacket is optional, but one that staff wear must carry the logo.
A jacket is compulsory, and the logo is optional.
Jackets and logos are both forbidden for staff.
repaso.feedback: El aviso no obliga a llevar chaqueta, pero impone una condición a quien la lleve: el logotipo.
repaso.texto: Notice to staff: wearing a name badge is required in all public areas. Staff are not forced to wear a jacket, but the regulations are clear that any jacket that staff wear at work must carry the company logo.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Llevar corbata es opcional, así que no tienes que llevarla.»
repaso.texto: The new rule leaves the choice to you. Wearing a tie is ___, so you don't have to wear one.
repaso.feedback: Optional describe lo que cada uno decide; don't have to confirma que no es obligatorio.

classes.objetivo: Redactar normas en lenguaje reglamentario con shall, may not, is/are to be y must be / may be + participio, y reconocer su equivalente informal.

ensenanza.en: Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with the terms printed on the back of the membership card.
ensenanza.es: Los usuarios devolverán todos los préstamos en un plazo de tres semanas, de acuerdo con las condiciones impresas en el reverso de la tarjeta de socio.
ensenanza.nota: Shall en un reglamento = obligación formal («deberán»); no es el shall de ofrecimiento (Shall I help?). In accordance with + norma: conforme a ella.

ensenanza.en: Membership cards may not be lent to another person, and any card found on the premises without its owner will be handed to the desk.
ensenanza.es: Las tarjetas de socio no podrán prestarse a otra persona, y toda tarjeta hallada en las instalaciones sin su titular se entregará en el mostrador.
ensenanza.nota: May not + be + participio: prohibición formal en pasiva; no se nombra a quien obedece. On the premises = dentro del local o edificio.

ensenanza.en: Overdue items are to be returned before the library closes, otherwise borrowers will be liable for a daily fine.
ensenanza.es: Los artículos con retraso se devolverán antes de que cierre la biblioteca; de lo contrario, los usuarios serán responsables de una multa diaria.
ensenanza.nota: Is/are to be + participio: orden oficial e impersonal. Be liable for + multa o daño: tener que pagarlo.

ensenanza.en: Damaged books must be reported to the staff at once, and no attempt should be made to repair them at home.
ensenanza.es: Los libros dañados deberán comunicarse al personal de inmediato, y no se intentará repararlos en casa.
ensenanza.nota: Must be + participio: obligación en pasiva; el libro es el sujeto. Report = comunicar, dar parte de algo.

ensenanza.en: Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book, but renewal is not granted for items that are already overdue.
ensenanza.es: Los préstamos podrán renovarse una vez, siempre que nadie haya reservado el libro, pero no se concede la renovación de los artículos que ya están con retraso.
ensenanza.nota: May be + participio: permiso formal en pasiva; provided that añade la condición. Renew = renovar.

ensenanza.en: Formal regulations avoid you and can't: they prefer shall and passive forms, so a notice on the wall may say that fines are to be paid at the desk.
ensenanza.es: Los reglamentos formales evitan you y can't: prefieren shall y las formas pasivas, así que un cartel en la pared puede decir que las multas se pagarán en el mostrador.
ensenanza.nota: El registro reglamentario es impersonal: sustituye you por el sujeto general (borrowers, users) y can't por may not.

explicacion.texto: Los reglamentos usan un registro formal e impersonal. Shall + verbo base expresa obligación (Borrowers shall return…); may not prohíbe; is/are to be + participio da una orden oficial; y must be o may be + participio expresan obligación o permiso sin nombrar a quien obedece. Evita will, can't o don't, que suenan a conversación. Este shall no es el de ofrecimiento (Shall I help you?) ni indica futuro: equivale al «deberá» de nuestros textos oficiales.

formula.nota: a quién va dirigida la norma
lo que se exige y el plazo

filas.texto: Bring late books to the desk.
Overdue items are to be returned.
You have to tell us about damage.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Borrowers shall to return all loans.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Shall, como los demás modales, va seguido del verbo base sin to.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Damaged books must report to the staff.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Damaged books must be reported to the staff.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Un libro no informa a nadie: con él como sujeto se necesita la pasiva must be + participio.

situacion.contexto: Sara trabaja en la biblioteca y le explica el reglamento a Carlos, un usuario nuevo.

dialogo.texto: The rules say that borrowers shall return loans within three weeks. Is that right?
dialogo.traduccion: El reglamento dice que los usuarios deberán devolver los préstamos en tres semanas. ¿Es correcto?

dialogo.texto: Yes. Overdue items are to be returned at the desk, and a fine applies.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Los artículos con retraso se devolverán en el mostrador y se aplica una multa.

dialogo.texto: Can I lend my membership card to my brother?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Puedo prestarle mi tarjeta de socio a mi hermano?

dialogo.texto: I'm afraid not. Membership cards may not be lent to another person.
dialogo.traduccion: Me temo que no. Las tarjetas de socio no podrán prestarse a otra persona.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué normas menciona Sara?

opciones.es: Devolver los préstamos en tres semanas y no prestar la tarjeta de socio.
Devolver en un mes y prestar la tarjeta a familiares.
Renovar cada semana y pagar al entrar.

item.feedback: Carlos cita el plazo de tres semanas y Sara añade que las tarjetas de socio «may not be lent» a otra persona.

guiada.consigna: Elige la versión formal de la primera norma del cartel.
opciones: Borrowers shall return books within three weeks.
Borrowers will bring back the books in three weeks.
Borrowers can return books within three weeks.
guiada.feedback: Shall + verbo base es la fórmula reglamentaria de obligación; will y can no fijan una obligación.
guiada.texto: Informal notice on the library door: You must return books in three weeks. You can't lend your card to anyone. Tell us if a book is damaged.
guiada.pista: Busca el modal que usan los reglamentos para obligar.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Los préstamos podrán renovarse una vez, salvo que el libro esté reservado.»
guiada.texto: Loans ___ be renewed once, unless the book has been reserved by another member.
guiada.feedback: May be + participio expresa el permiso formal en pasiva; unless añade la excepción.
guiada.pista: Es el modal formal de permiso, más reglamentario que can.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Los bolsos se dejarán en la entrada.»
guiada.respuesta: Bags are to be left at the entrance
guiada.feedback: Are to be + participio da una orden oficial sin nombrar a quien la cumple.
guiada.pista: Are to be + participio: orden impersonal.

practica.consigna: Escucha el aviso y elige qué debe hacer quien quiera renovar un préstamo.
practica.audio: Good morning, and welcome to the library. A few words about how things work here. Borrowers shall return all loans within three weeks, in accordance with the terms printed on your membership card. Overdue items are to be returned at the desk, and borrowers will be liable for a small daily fine. Loans may be renewed once, provided that nobody has reserved the book. Damaged books must be reported to the staff, and no food or drink may be taken into the reading room on any account.
opciones: Make sure nobody else has reserved the book.
Pay a small fine in advance at the desk.
Return it first and borrow it again at once.
practica.feedback: La renovación se concede solo una vez y a condición de que nadie haya reservado el libro («provided that nobody has reserved»).

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada norma formal con su función.
pares: Borrowers shall register at the desk.
Food may not be eaten in the reading room.
Overdue items are to be returned at once.
practica.feedback: Shall obliga en activa, may not prohíbe, may be permite y are to be da una orden oficial.

practica.consigna: Lee el aviso: ¿qué tono y propósito tiene?
opciones: Formal and firm: it announces an official rule with a consequence.
Friendly: it invites readers to show their cards only if they wish.
Apologetic: it regrets that the library must close.
practica.feedback: Usa shall y anuncia una consecuencia para quien no cumpla: es una norma formal y firme, no una sugerencia.
practica.texto: Library notice: from Monday, all users must show their membership card at the desk on request. Borrowers who do not do so shall be asked to leave the premises. This rule is introduced in accordance with the new safety regulations, and it applies to all users without exception.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha a la bibliotecaria y elige qué no puede hacerse con los libros de consulta.
evaluacion.audio: A librarian is explaining the rules to a new member. Reference books may not be taken out of the room, she says, although readers may copy a few pages by hand. Loans shall be limited to five items at a time, and overdue items are to be returned before any new loan is granted. If a book is damaged, the borrower should report it at once: nobody will be liable for damage that was reported honestly.
opciones: Taking them out of the room.
Copying a few pages by hand.
Borrowing five of them at a time.
evaluacion.feedback: «May not be taken out of the room» prohíbe sacar los libros de consulta; copiar páginas a mano sí se permite.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud adopta ella ante quien avisa de un daño?
evaluacion.audio: A librarian is explaining the rules to a new member. Reference books may not be taken out of the room, she says, although readers may copy a few pages by hand. Loans shall be limited to five items at a time, and overdue items are to be returned before any new loan is granted. If a book is damaged, the borrower should report it at once: nobody will be liable for damage that was reported honestly.
opciones: She is kind to users who report damage.
She will fine anyone who damages a book.
She insists that users repair the damage themselves.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice que nadie será responsable de un daño comunicado con honestidad: es comprensiva con quien avisa.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los libros dañados deberán comunicarse al personal de inmediato.»
evaluacion.texto: Please do not try to repair anything yourself. Damaged books must be ___ to the staff at once.
evaluacion.feedback: Must be + participio forma la obligación en pasiva; reported es el participio de report.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Las multas se pagarán en el mostrador antes de las cinco.»
evaluacion.respuesta: Fines are to be paid at the desk before five
evaluacion.feedback: Are to be + participio da una orden oficial impersonal; before five fija el plazo.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué postura defiende la bibliotecaria sobre el lenguaje formal?
repaso.audio: At a committee meeting, the head librarian proposed changing the wording of the rules. Notices that say you must or you can't, she argued, sound like orders from a teacher, whereas borrowers shall and cards may not be lent sound like official rules, and people take them seriously. Her colleague disagreed: he thought that formal wording makes readers nervous, and he preferred a friendlier tone.
opciones: That formal wording gives rules more weight.
That friendly wording is always better.
That rules should not be written down.
repaso.feedback: Defiende que las fórmulas formales suenan a norma oficial y por eso la gente las toma en serio; su colega opina lo contrario.

repaso.consigna: Lee la nota: ¿qué se deduce sobre los cobros por daños?
opciones: They cannot be charged until the manager approves each case.
They are charged automatically to every borrower who is late.
They are the responsibility of the staff member.
repaso.feedback: La nota dice que no se cobrará a nadie hasta que la dirección apruebe cada caso: el cobro depende de esa aprobación.
repaso.texto: To all staff: with effect from Monday, overdue notices are to be sent by email and not by post. Damaged items shall be recorded on the new form, and no borrower may be asked to pay anything until the manager has approved each case.

repaso.consigna: Escribe la norma formal sobre la tarjeta de socio.
repaso.texto: Escribe en inglés formal: los usuarios deberán mostrar su tarjeta de socio al personal.
repaso.respuesta: Users shall show their membership card to the staff.
aceptadas: Users must show their membership card to the staff.
Membership cards are to be shown to the staff.
Membership cards must be shown to the staff.
Users are to show their membership cards to the staff.
Users shall show their membership cards to the staff.
repaso.feedback: Shall + verbo base (o la pasiva are to be shown) da la obligación formal que exige un reglamento.

classes.objetivo: Comprender un debate público: identificar quién decide, quién se beneficia y cuál es la razón de una norma, distinguir intención de impacto y reconocer lo que se encarga a terceros (have + objeto + participio).

ensenanza.en: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.
ensenanza.es: El ayuntamiento decide las normas, pero los vecinos son quienes viven con ellas cada día, y rara vez tienen voz real en el resultado.
ensenanza.nota: Quien decide y quien soporta la decisión son papeles distintos. Have a say: tener voz en una decisión.

ensenanza.en: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and several of them have a vested interest in how it turns out.
ensenanza.es: Comerciantes, padres y ciclistas son partes interesadas en el nuevo plan de tráfico, y varios tienen un interés personal en cómo acabe.
ensenanza.nota: Stakeholder: quien se ve afectado por una decisión aunque no la tome. Vested interest: interés propio, a menudo económico.

ensenanza.en: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.
ensenanza.es: ¿Quién se beneficiará de la nueva norma y quién la pagará? Un buen debate siempre plantea ambas preguntas antes de votar.
ensenanza.nota: Benefit from + norma: quien gana. Se contrasta con who pays, que señala a quien soporta el coste.

ensenanza.en: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.
ensenanza.es: La razón de fondo es sencilla: menos coches significan calles más seguras cerca del colegio, aunque una norma que ayuda a unos puede ir a costa de otros.
ensenanza.nota: Rationale: la razón que justifica la norma. At the expense of + personas o cosas: perjudicándolas para beneficiar a otros.

ensenanza.en: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.
ensenanza.es: El ayuntamiento sostiene que la prohibición pretende proteger a los niños, pero su impacto en los comercios podría ser serio; una consecuencia no prevista es un efecto que nadie había planeado.
ensenanza.nota: Intended to = la intención; impact = el efecto real, que puede ser distinto. Unintended consequence: lo que pasa sin que nadie lo buscara.

ensenanza.en: The council has the park benches painted by a contractor every spring, which means it pays for the work but does not do it.
ensenanza.es: El ayuntamiento hace que un contratista pinte los bancos del parque cada primavera, lo que significa que paga el trabajo pero no lo hace.
ensenanza.nota: Have + objeto + participio: encargas el trabajo a otro; tú no lo haces. Contractor: empresa o persona contratada.

explicacion.titulo: Quién decide, quién gana y por qué
explicacion.texto: Para seguir un debate público pregúntate tres cosas: ¿quién decide? (the council), ¿quién se ve afectado? (residents, stakeholders) y ¿por qué? (the rationale: because, so that). Distingue la intención (intended to) del impacto (the impact on…): una norma puede buscar un bien y causar un problema. Cuando alguien encarga una tarea a un tercero, el inglés usa have + objeto + participio: The council has the benches painted (no los pinta él).

patron.texto: Quién decide + qué decide + razón (intended to):

formula.texto: because the ban is intended to protect children.

filas.texto: the council · the committee · the mayor
rationale · because · so that · intended to

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The council has the bins to be emptied every Monday.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The council has the bins emptied every Monday.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras have + objeto va el participio, sin to ni be.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Who benefits of the new rule?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Who benefits from the new rule?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Benefit se construye con from, no con of.

situacion.contexto: Ana y Carlos siguen un debate del ayuntamiento sobre cerrar al tráfico la calle del colegio.

dialogo.texto: The council wants to close the school street to cars. Who will benefit?
dialogo.traduccion: El ayuntamiento quiere cerrar la calle del colegio a los coches. ¿Quién saldrá ganando?

dialogo.texto: Families, mostly. The rationale is that fewer cars mean safer streets.
dialogo.traduccion: Las familias, sobre todo. La razón es que menos coches significan calles más seguras.

dialogo.texto: But the shop owners argue that the impact on their business will be serious.
dialogo.traduccion: Pero los comerciantes sostienen que el impacto en su negocio será serio.

dialogo.texto: True. The council has already chosen a contractor, but nobody has asked the shops.
dialogo.traduccion: Cierto. El ayuntamiento ya ha elegido a un contratista, pero nadie ha preguntado a las tiendas.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿quién decide y qué temen los comerciantes?

opciones.es: Decide el ayuntamiento; los comerciantes temen un impacto serio en su negocio.
Deciden los comerciantes; las familias temen un impacto serio.
Decide un contratista; los comerciantes esperan ganar clientes.

item.feedback: Ana dice que el ayuntamiento quiere cerrar la calle y que los comerciantes «argue that the impact on their business will be serious».

guiada.consigna: Escucha y elige quién toma la decisión.
guiada.audio: The council voted last night to close Mill Street to cars during school hours. Residents and shop owners both spoke at the meeting, but only the council members took the vote.
opciones: The council.
The residents.
The shop owners.
guiada.feedback: El verbo voted y el sujeto the council indican quién decide; vecinos y comerciantes solo hablaron en la reunión.
guiada.pista: El decisor es quien vota o aprueba la norma, no quien habla en la reunión.

guiada.consigna: Según el texto, ¿quién se beneficia de la norma?
opciones: Parents, because the streets will be safer.
Shop owners, because they will sell more.
The council, because it will earn money.
guiada.feedback: Los padres ganan calles más seguras; los comerciantes temen un impacto negativo y el ayuntamiento habla de seguridad, no de beneficios.
guiada.texto: Parents welcome the ban because fewer cars mean safer streets near the school. Shop owners fear the impact on their sales, and the council says the rationale is safety, not profit.
guiada.pista: Busca el grupo que recibe un efecto positivo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «¿Quién se beneficiará de esta norma y quién la pagará?»
guiada.texto: Every new rule helps some people and costs others. Who will ___ from this one, and who will pay for it?
guiada.feedback: Benefit from + norma señala a quien gana con ella; se contrasta con quien paga.
guiada.pista: Es el verbo que significa «beneficiarse» y va con from.

practica.consigna: Escucha la reunión y elige qué objeción plantea el vecino.
practica.audio: At a public meeting, the council's spokesperson explained the plan. The rationale, she said, is simple: the bus lane is intended to cut journey times, so commuters will benefit most. Then a shop owner spoke. He agreed with the aim, but argued that parking is how his customers reach him, so the impact on his business would be serious. A resident added that nobody had asked the people who live on the street. The spokesperson replied that the council had chosen a contractor to study the traffic, and that the results would be published before the final vote.
opciones: That nobody asked the people on the street.
That the contractor costs too much for the council.
That the bus lane is too short for the street.
practica.feedback: El vecino dice que nadie preguntó a quienes viven en la calle; el comercio teme por el aparcamiento y el contratista solo estudia el tráfico.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión del debate con su significado.
practica.feedback: El contractor ejecuta un encargo, los stakeholders son los afectados, un vested interest es un interés propio y una unintended consequence no estaba prevista.

practica.consigna: Lee el artículo: ¿qué quiere ilustrar el autor con el ejemplo?
opciones: That intention and impact can differ greatly.
That the mayor acted in bad faith.
That litter was never a real problem.
practica.feedback: El alcalde buscaba reducir la basura, pero el problema se trasladó a otras calles: la intención y el impacto no coinciden.
practica.texto: The mayor insists that the ban is intended to reduce litter, but after three months complaints have doubled, because people now leave rubbish in the side streets. Nobody wanted that outcome. It shows how a rule can work on paper and go wrong in practice, and why the people affected should be heard before, not after.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha a la vecina y elige quién saldría ganando con la tasa de aparcamiento.
evaluacion.audio: Ms Park, a resident, spoke for two minutes at the council. She said she was not against the new parking charge in principle; what worried her was who would pay. Drivers who come into town would benefit from emptier streets, she said, but the workers who live nearby would pay, at the expense of their own family budgets. She asked the council to show the evidence for its rationale before the vote. The mayor thanked her, but did not promise any change.
opciones: Drivers who come into town.
Workers who live on the street.
Families of the council members.
evaluacion.feedback: La vecina dice que quienes vienen en coche a la ciudad se beneficiarían de calles más vacías, mientras que los trabajadores del barrio pagarían.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud muestra la vecina hacia la norma?
evaluacion.audio: Ms Park, a resident, spoke for two minutes at the council. She said she was not against the new parking charge in principle; what worried her was who would pay. Drivers who come into town would benefit from emptier streets, she said, but the workers who live nearby would pay, at the expense of their own family budgets. She asked the council to show the evidence for its rationale before the vote. The mayor thanked her, but did not promise any change.
opciones: She accepts the idea but asks who pays.
She rejects any kind of charge in principle.
She supports the plan without any reservations.
evaluacion.feedback: No está en contra de la tasa en principio («not against»), pero cuestiona quién la paga y pide pruebas: acepta la idea y critica el reparto del coste.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El ayuntamiento no pinta los bancos; hace que los pinte un contratista.»
evaluacion.texto: The council does not paint the benches itself. It has the benches ___ by a contractor every spring.
evaluacion.feedback: Have + objeto + participio (painted) expresa que el trabajo lo hace otro.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Los comerciantes sostienen que el impacto será serio.»
evaluacion.respuesta: Shop owners argue that the impact will be serious
evaluacion.feedback: Argue that + oración introduce la postura de un grupo; impact es el efecto real de la norma.

repaso.consigna: Escucha la entrevista: ¿qué reconoce la representante del ayuntamiento?
repaso.audio: In a radio interview, a council member defended the ban on cars near the school. The intention, she said, was never to hurt shops, but to protect children at the school gates. When the interviewer pointed out that two shops had already closed, she admitted that nobody had predicted that effect, and promised a review within six months.
opciones: That the rule had an effect nobody expected.
That the rule was a mistake from the start.
That the shops are to blame for closing.
repaso.feedback: Admite que nadie había previsto el cierre de las tiendas: una consecuencia no prevista, y promete revisar la norma.

repaso.consigna: Lee la carta: ¿con qué propósito la escribe el vecino?
opciones: To demand a say before any decision.
To thank the council for its work.
To ask the contractor to finish sooner.
repaso.feedback: Se queja de que los vecinos se enteran después y pide hablar con los afectados antes de decidir.
repaso.texto: I have lived on this street for thirty years, and I am tired of hearing that we are all stakeholders. The council decides, the contractor builds, and residents are told afterwards. If the rationale is good, it will not be afraid of a conversation with the people who live here.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Quien posee los locales tiene un interés personal en la norma.»
repaso.texto: A landlord who owns several shops on the street has a ___ interest in how the rule turns out.
repaso.feedback: Vested interest es el interés propio, normalmente económico, que alguien tiene en un resultado.

classes.objetivo: Redactar normas justas con pasivas modales (must be, may only be, are to be), excepciones (except, apart from), condiciones (on condition that) y una razón breve (in order to, given that).

vocabulario.es: alegando que, por el motivo de que

ensenanza.en: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, which the committee has marked with a green sign at each entrance.
ensenanza.es: Los perros deberán llevarse con correa, salvo en la zona vallada, que el comité ha señalado con un cartel verde en cada entrada.
ensenanza.nota: Except + lugar, tiempo o persona: introduce la excepción. Must be kept: obligación en pasiva.

ensenanza.en: Fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily, so the committee considers a blanket ban elsewhere fair.
ensenanza.es: Las hogueras solo podrán encenderse en la zona señalada, dado que la hierba seca arde con facilidad, por lo que el comité considera justa una prohibición general en el resto.
ensenanza.nota: Given that + oración: da la razón de la norma. Blanket ban: prohibición que se aplica a todos y a todo, sin matices.

ensenanza.en: Bicycles are to be left at the racks in order to keep the paths clear, and the committee may make an exception for deliveries.
ensenanza.es: Las bicicletas se dejarán en los soportes para mantener despejados los caminos, y el comité podrá hacer una excepción para los repartos.
ensenanza.nota: In order to + verbo: la finalidad de la norma. Make an exception: permitir algo que normalmente no se permite.

ensenanza.en: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, which is a fair test and easy to apply.
ensenanza.es: Se podrá poner música siempre que no moleste a otros visitantes, lo que es un criterio justo y fácil de aplicar.
ensenanza.nota: On condition that + presente: condición formal, más fuerte que if. Fair = justo, equilibrado.

ensenanza.en: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the playground, on the grounds that small children could be frightened; it is the only exception.
ensenanza.es: Salvo los perros guía, ningún animal podrá entrar en el área de juegos, alegando que los niños pequeños podrían asustarse; es la única excepción.
ensenanza.nota: Apart from + nombre: excepción. On the grounds that + oración: el motivo que se alega para justificar la regla.

ensenanza.en: A fair rule has a clear reason, a reasonable exception and a responsible person, and the committee will draft it in plain language.
ensenanza.es: Una norma justa tiene una razón clara, una excepción razonable y un responsable, y el comité la redactará en un lenguaje sencillo.
ensenanza.nota: Una buena norma tiene razón, excepción razonable y responsable claro. Draft = redactar un borrador.

explicacion.texto: Una norma bien redactada tiene cuatro piezas: la regla (Dogs must be kept on a lead), una excepción (except in the fenced area; apart from guide dogs), una condición (on condition that, unless) y una razón (in order to, so as to, given that, on the grounds that). Las pasivas (must be kept, may only be lit, are to be left) evitan nombrar a quien obedece y suenan oficiales. Tras except y apart from se usa un nombre o un lugar; tras given that y on condition that, una oración completa. Una blanket ban rara vez es justa: por eso se suele hacer una excepción razonable.

formula.texto: Dogs must be kept on a lead,
in order to protect other visitors.

filas.texto: must be · may only be · are to be + participio
in order to · so as to · given that · since

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Dogs must keep on a lead in the park.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Dogs must be kept on a lead in the park.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: El perro no se controla a sí mismo: la regla necesita la pasiva must be kept.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Except of guide dogs, no animals may enter.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Except for guide dogs, no animals may enter.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Except se une a un nombre con for (o se usa apart from); nunca con of.

situacion.contexto: Leo y Sara, del comité del barrio, redactan las reglas de un parque nuevo.

dialogo.texto: Draft rule one: dogs must be kept on a lead.
dialogo.traduccion: Borrador de la regla uno: los perros deberán llevarse con correa.

dialogo.texto: Fair, but let's add an exception for the fenced area, since dogs need space to run.
dialogo.traduccion: Justo, pero añadamos una excepción para la zona vallada, ya que los perros necesitan espacio para correr.

dialogo.texto: Agreed. And music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors.
dialogo.traduccion: De acuerdo. Y se podrá poner música siempre que no moleste a otros visitantes.

dialogo.texto: Good. Every rule needs a reason in order to be fair.
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. Cada norma necesita una razón para ser justa.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué incluyen las reglas del parque?

opciones.es: Perros con correa salvo en la zona vallada, y música con la condición de no molestar.
Perros siempre con correa y música prohibida.
Perros libres salvo en el camino, y música sin condiciones.

item.feedback: Leo propone la correa y Sara añade la excepción de la zona vallada; Leo completa con la música «on condition that it does not disturb».

guiada.consigna: Elige la regla bien redactada con una excepción.
opciones: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area.
Dogs must keep on a lead, except in the fenced area.
Dogs must be kept on a lead, except of the fenced area.
guiada.feedback: Must be kept es la pasiva correcta y except + lugar introduce la excepción; las otras opciones rompen la pasiva o usan except of.
guiada.texto: The committee wants dogs on a lead in the park, but it accepts one exception: the fenced area, where dogs can run freely.
guiada.pista: La regla necesita la pasiva: modal + be + participio.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Se permitirán picnics siempre que se lleven la basura a casa.»
guiada.texto: The committee wants the park to stay clean. Picnics are permitted on ___ that visitors take their rubbish home.
guiada.feedback: On condition that + oración es la fórmula formal de condición.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo que sigue a on en la fórmula formal de condición.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Salvo los perros guía, ningún animal podrá entrar en los jardines.»
guiada.respuesta: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the gardens
guiada.feedback: Apart from + nombre abre la excepción y después llega la regla general.
guiada.pista: La excepción abre la frase: Apart from…

practica.consigna: Escucha la reunión: ¿a quién se aplica la excepción de las bicicletas?
practica.audio: At the committee meeting, the chair read out the draft of the new park rules. Dogs must be kept on a lead, she said, except in the fenced area, given that they need space to run. Fires may only be lit in the marked area, and then only with an adult present. Loud music is not banned completely; it may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors. One member objected that a blanket ban on bicycles would be unfair, so the committee agreed to make an exception for children under ten.
opciones: Children under ten.
People making deliveries.
Adults with a special card.
practica.feedback: El comité evita la prohibición general de bicicletas haciendo una excepción para los menores de diez años.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada fragmento con la pieza de la norma que cumple.
pares: given that dry grass burns easily
on condition that the area is left clean
Bicycles are to be left at the racks
practica.feedback: Apart from marca una excepción, given that una razón, on condition that una condición y are to be left la regla.

practica.consigna: Lee el aviso: ¿qué postura refleja el comité?
opciones: It looks for a compromise rather than a complete ban.
It bans dogs completely to protect children.
It lets dogs run free to please their owners.
practica.feedback: Rechaza la prohibición total y propone correa con una zona de excepción: busca un equilibrio entre vecinos con perros y con niños.
practica.texto: Notice from the committee: after a long discussion, we decided against a blanket ban on dogs. Instead, dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area. We believe this is a fair balance, given that many residents have dogs and others have small children. The rule will be reviewed after six months.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el debate y elige qué propone la profesora de música.
evaluacion.audio: In a community meeting, one neighbour proposed a blanket ban on loud music in the park. Another neighbour, a music teacher, disagreed: she thought the rule should allow music on condition that it stops at nine, given that many families use the park in the evening. The chair suggested combining both ideas, and then asked each speaker to write one sentence that included a reason, so that the committee could compare the proposals fairly.
opciones: Allowing music, but only until nine.
Banning music at all times.
Allowing music all night long.
evaluacion.feedback: Propone permitir la música a condición de que termine a las nueve, en lugar de una prohibición general.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha otra vez: ¿por qué pide el presidente una frase con razón a cada uno?
evaluacion.audio: In a community meeting, one neighbour proposed a blanket ban on loud music in the park. Another neighbour, a music teacher, disagreed: she thought the rule should allow music on condition that it stops at nine, given that many families use the park in the evening. The chair suggested combining both ideas, and then asked each speaker to write one sentence that included a reason, so that the committee could compare the proposals fairly.
opciones: To compare the proposals on equal terms.
To reject both proposals at once.
To decide who should speak first.
evaluacion.feedback: Pedir una razón a cada uno permite al comité comparar las propuestas en igualdad de condiciones («so that the committee could compare the proposals fairly»).

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Dado que la hierba seca arde con facilidad, se prohíben las hogueras.»
evaluacion.texto: The summer has been very dry. ___ that the grass burns easily, fires are prohibited.
evaluacion.feedback: Given that + oración introduce la razón de la norma.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tres normas para un parque comunitario con excepciones y una razón.
evaluacion.texto: Eres miembro del comité de un parque comunitario con un área de juegos, un estanque y un camino principal. Escribe tres normas (entre 130 y 200 palabras en total). Cada una lleva una regla en pasiva (must be, may only be, are to be), una excepción o condición (except, apart from, unless, on condition that) y una razón (in order to, given that, since, so as to).
evaluacion.respuesta: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.
aceptadas: First, rubbish must be taken home, except on festival days, because the bins are full by noon and the park looks dirty for the next visitors. Second, fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily and a single spark could close the whole park for a week. Third, dogs are to be kept on a lead, apart from guide dogs, in order to keep the playground safe for small children, who are often afraid of big animals. Finally, the gates shall be locked at ten unless the committee has approved an event, since neighbours need quiet at night. These rules are fair, because each one has a reason.
evaluacion.feedback: Una norma justa une una regla en pasiva, una excepción o condición razonable y una razón que la justifique (in order to, given that, since).

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué quiere decir la presidenta con su última frase?
repaso.audio: After the meeting, the chair summarised why the rules were written the way they were. The aim, she said, was not to ban but to balance: dogs on leads except in the fenced area, music on condition that it ends early, and bicycles allowed apart from on the main path. She added that a rule without a reason is just an order, and people only follow orders while someone is watching.
opciones: That rules with clear reasons are more likely to be followed.
That rules should work only while people are being watched.
That orders work better than explained rules.
repaso.feedback: Dice que una norma sin razón es solo una orden y que se obedece únicamente mientras alguien vigila: las normas razonadas se respetan mejor.

repaso.consigna: Lee el correo: ¿qué pide el vecino?
opciones: A wider exception to the dog rule at weekends.
The end of the dog rule completely.
A blanket ban on big dogs.
repaso.feedback: Acepta la norma, pero pide ampliar la excepción de la zona vallada los fines de semana.
repaso.texto: Dear committee, I agree with the new dog rule in principle, but I think the exception is too narrow. The fenced area is small, and on busy days it is unsafe for big dogs. Could you consider making it bigger, at least at weekends? I would be happy to help measure the space.

repaso.consigna: Escribe una norma formal sobre las hogueras con una excepción.
repaso.texto: Escribe una norma formal: las hogueras solo podrán encenderse en la zona señalada.
repaso.respuesta: Fires may only be lit in the marked area.
aceptadas: Fires may not be lit, except in the marked area.
Fires are to be lit only in the marked area.
Fires must only be lit in the marked area.
Fires may be lit only in the marked area.
Fires are not to be lit except in the marked area.
repaso.feedback: May only be + participio expresa un permiso restringido en pasiva, sin nombrar a quien obedece.

classes.objetivo: Integrar obligación, prohibición, lenguaje reglamentario, razón y excepciones para redactar una normativa breve y un aviso cercano que la explique a los vecinos.

ensenanza.en: This policy sets out the rules for using the shared garden, and it will take effect on the first of May for every plot holder.
ensenanza.es: Esta normativa establece las reglas para usar el huerto compartido y entrará en vigor el uno de mayo para todos los titulares de parcela.
ensenanza.nota: Policy: el documento que reúne las normas; se redacta en presente formal. Take effect: entrar en vigor en una fecha.

ensenanza.en: Each member shall keep their plot free of weeds, and any plot left untended for two months may be offered to someone on the waiting list.
ensenanza.es: Cada socio mantendrá su parcela libre de malas hierbas, y toda parcela abandonada durante dos meses podrá ofrecerse a alguien de la lista de espera.
ensenanza.nota: Each + singular + shall + verbo base: obligación formal y directa; each no lleva -s.

ensenanza.en: Tools are to be cleaned and returned to the shed after use, and members who damage them will be held accountable for the repair.
ensenanza.es: Las herramientas se limpiarán y se devolverán al cobertizo después de usarse, y los socios que las dañen responderán de la reparación.
ensenanza.nota: Are to be + participio: orden impersonal de reglamento. Be held accountable: asumir las consecuencias de algo.

ensenanza.en: Compost may be taken home, provided that it is shared fairly, in the interest of all the neighbours who help to make it.
ensenanza.es: Se podrá llevar compost a casa, siempre que se reparta de forma justa, en interés de todos los vecinos que ayudan a hacerlo.
ensenanza.nota: May be + participio con una condición: permiso formal con límite. In the interest of + personas: en beneficio de ellas.

ensenanza.en: The committee has the paths cleaned by a company, but each member is responsible for their own plot and for watering it on their rota day.
ensenanza.es: El comité hace limpiar los caminos a una empresa, pero cada socio es responsable de su parcela y de regarla el día que le toque en el turno.
ensenanza.nota: Have + objeto + participio: se encarga a un tercero. Responsible for: quien responde de la tarea. Rota: el turno que reparte las tareas.

ensenanza.en: Dear neighbours, this public notice explains why the garden will be closed on Mondays, and what each of you needs to do about it.
ensenanza.es: Estimados vecinos, este aviso público explica por qué el huerto cerrará los lunes y qué debe hacer cada uno de ustedes al respecto.
ensenanza.nota: Un aviso abre con el destinatario y da pronto el motivo, en tono cercano; el mismo contenido que la normativa, dicho de otro modo.

explicacion.titulo: De la normativa al aviso para los vecinos
explicacion.texto: Una normativa y un aviso dicen lo mismo con dos tonos. La normativa es formal e impersonal (shall, may not, are to be + participio) y enumera reglas, excepciones y responsables. El aviso para los vecinos explica la misma decisión de forma cercana: saluda (Dear neighbours), da la razón (because, in order to, given that), resume lo que cambia y dice a quién acudir. Antes de escribir pregúntate quién decide, quién se ve afectado y por qué.

patron.texto: Regla formal → explicación cercana para los vecinos:

formula.texto: Each member shall keep their plot tidy.
formula.nota: normativa: shall + verbo base, tono formal

formula.texto: Dear neighbours, every member will keep their plot tidy
in order to keep the garden nice for everybody.
formula.nota: la razón que justifica la norma

filas.texto: Tools are to be returned to the shed.
Please return the tools to the shed.
You are welcome to take compost home.
Members shall not water after noon.
We ask members not to water after noon.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Dear neighbours, we are writing for inform you about the new rules.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Dear neighbours, we are writing to inform you about the new rules.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La finalidad se expresa con to + verbo; for + verbo no existe en inglés.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Each members shall keep their plot tidy.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Each member shall keep their plot tidy.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Each va seguido de un nombre en singular, sin -s.

situacion.contexto: La comisión de un huerto comunitario explica la normativa a una vecina nueva, Mia.

dialogo.texto: Do I have to keep my plot free of weeds?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Tengo que mantener mi parcela libre de malas hierbas?

dialogo.texto: Yes. Each member shall keep their plot tidy, apart from the flower corner.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Cada socio mantendrá su parcela ordenada, salvo el rincón de las flores.

dialogo.texto: And the tools?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y las herramientas?

dialogo.texto: Tools are to be cleaned and returned to the shed. The rota says who waters on which day.
dialogo.traduccion: Las herramientas se limpiarán y se devolverán al cobertizo. El turno dice quién riega cada día.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué debe hacer Mia y qué queda fuera de la regla?

opciones.es: Mantener su parcela ordenada, salvo el rincón de las flores, y devolver las herramientas limpias.
Cuidar solo el rincón de las flores y dejar las herramientas fuera.
Regar cada día sin turno y llevarse las herramientas a casa.

item.feedback: Tom dice que cada socio mantiene su parcela ordenada, «apart from the flower corner», y que las herramientas se limpian y se devuelven al cobertizo.

guiada.consigna: Elige la versión formal de la regla para una normativa.
opciones: Each member shall keep the shed locked.
Each member will keep the shed locked, OK?
Every member keeps to lock the shed.
guiada.feedback: Each member shall + verbo base es la fórmula de obligación de una normativa; las otras dos son informales o incorrectas.
guiada.texto: The committee is drafting its policy for the shared garden. The informal rule on the wall says: please lock the shed when you leave.
guiada.pista: Busca el modal formal y el sujeto en singular.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Los socios son responsables de regar su propia parcela.»
guiada.texto: Nobody else will water your plot for you. Members are ___ for watering their own plots.
guiada.feedback: Responsible for + -ing indica quién responde de una tarea.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo que significa «responsable» y se une a for.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Estimados vecinos, les escribimos para informarles del cambio.»
guiada.respuesta: Dear neighbours, we are writing to inform you of the change
guiada.feedback: El aviso abre con el destinatario y expresa la finalidad con to + verbo: to inform.
aceptadas: Dear neighbours, we are writing to inform you about the change
guiada.pista: Tras el saludo, la finalidad va con to + verbo.

practica.consigna: Escucha el aviso y elige por qué cerrarán el huerto los lunes.
practica.audio: Good evening, neighbours. From next month, the garden will be closed on Mondays, because the soil needs to rest. The decision was taken by the committee in the interest of all members, and it will take effect on the first of May. Members may still collect their tools on Mondays, provided that they ask the rota manager first. Anyone who leaves a plot untended for two months will be held accountable, and the plot may be offered to someone on the waiting list. If you have questions, please come to the meeting on Saturday morning.
opciones: To let the soil rest.
To repair the shed.
To stop neighbours from visiting.
practica.feedback: La razón del cierre es que la tierra necesita descansar; los socios aún pueden recoger herramientas con permiso.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con su tono o su función.
pares: Tools are to be returned to the shed.
Please return the tools to the shed.
Dear neighbours, we are writing to explain…
The new rule will take effect in May.
practica.feedback: Are to be es formal y please suena cercano; Dear neighbours abre un aviso y take effect fija cuándo empieza a valer la norma.

opciones: Understanding but firm: it explains a hard decision.
Cold and legal: it only lists penalties.
Apologetic: it cancels the decision.
practica.feedback: Reconoce que la decisión será dura, pero la mantiene y la explica con la lista de espera: comprensivo y firme.
practica.texto: Dear neighbours, we are writing to explain why plots will no longer be handed down within a family. The committee knows this will be hard for some of you, but the waiting list now has forty names, and it would not be fair to make them wait for ever. We hope you will understand, and we are ready to talk to anyone who is affected.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la reunión y elige cuál es la razón de la nueva normativa.
evaluacion.audio: Ms Ortiz, from the garden committee, explained the new policy. Our rationale is simple, she said: plots should be shared fairly. The waiting list is long, so each family will be limited to one plot. Mr Bell, a member with three children, replied that he understood the aim, but that the impact on large families would be serious. Ms Ortiz answered that the committee would listen to any family that felt treated unfairly, but she would not promise an exception.
opciones: To share plots more fairly.
To raise the price of plots.
To give large families more space.
evaluacion.feedback: La razón es la justicia: como la lista de espera es larga, se limita una parcela por familia.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué da a entender la Sra. Ortiz al no prometer una excepción?
evaluacion.audio: Ms Ortiz, from the garden committee, explained the new policy. Our rationale is simple, she said: plots should be shared fairly. The waiting list is long, so each family will be limited to one plot. Mr Bell, a member with three children, replied that he understood the aim, but that the impact on large families would be serious. Ms Ortiz answered that the committee would listen to any family that felt treated unfairly, but she would not promise an exception.
opciones: She will listen, but does not want to raise false hopes.
She has already rejected every complaint.
She will make exceptions for any large family.
evaluacion.feedback: Se ofrece a escuchar pero no promete nada: no quiere crear falsas esperanzas, sin cerrar la puerta a hablar.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los socios que dañen las herramientas responderán del coste.»
evaluacion.texto: Please take care of the tools. Members who damage them will be held ___ for the cost.
evaluacion.feedback: Be held accountable for significa responder de algo, con las consecuencias que eso implique.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una normativa breve y un aviso para los vecinos.
evaluacion.texto: Eres secretario o secretaria del comité de un huerto comunitario. Escribe en inglés, en un solo texto de 140 a 200 palabras: (1) varias normas formales (shall, may not, are to be) con una excepción o condición y (2) un aviso cercano para los vecinos (Dear neighbours) que explique la razón de la normativa.
evaluacion.respuesta: Policy: Each member shall keep their plot free of weeds. Tools are to be cleaned and returned to the shed after use, and members who damage them will be held accountable. Compost may be taken home, provided that it is shared fairly. Dogs may not enter the garden, except for guide dogs. Notice: Dear neighbours, we are writing to explain the new garden policy, which will take effect in May. The rules are intended to keep the garden nice for everybody, given that so many families share it. Each member is responsible for watering on their rota day, but you don't have to work on other days. In order to keep the tools safe, please return them to the shed. We know that change is never easy, and we thank you for your understanding. If you have any questions, please speak to the committee on Saturday morning.
aceptadas: Policy: Every member shall pay a small fee each year. Plots must be kept tidy, and weeds are to be removed every week. Fires may not be lit in the garden, apart from the barbecue area. Notice: Dear neighbours, from May the garden has a new policy. Its rationale is fairness, since a long waiting list means that nobody should leave a plot empty. Members are responsible for telling the committee if they cannot look after their plot, and anyone who ignores a rule will be held accountable. You are permitted to bring friends on Sundays, provided that they follow the rules. Please speak to us if anything is unclear. Thank you for your help, and we hope you will enjoy the garden.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen texto separa dos registros: normas formales e impersonales y un aviso cercano que saluda, da la razón y dice a quién acudir.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué actitud muestra el socio al final?
repaso.audio: After the meeting, a member complained that the new rule had been announced too late. The chair agreed that the notice could have gone out earlier, but she pointed out that the rule takes effect only in May, which gives everyone time to prepare. She added that a notice that explains the reason is always better than one that simply gives an order. The member did not look convinced.
opciones: He stays unhappy despite the explanation.
He is now fully satisfied with the plan.
He is angry at the chair personally.
repaso.feedback: La presidenta da sus razones, pero el socio «no parecía convencido»: sigue sin aceptar la explicación.

repaso.consigna: Lee el correo: ¿qué actitud muestra el comité ante las críticas?
opciones: It accepts objections, but only through a formal route.
It refuses to hear any objections at all.
It invites everyone to ignore the new limit.
repaso.feedback: Invita a presentar la objeción por escrito antes de fin de mes: acepta críticas, pero por un cauce formal.
repaso.texto: To all plot holders: with effect from the first of May, compost may only be taken home in the interest of fair sharing, and each household may take no more than two bags a week. The committee has not taken this decision lightly. If you think the limit is unfair, please put your case in writing before the end of the month.

repaso.consigna: Escribe una frase amable pidiendo devolver las herramientas.
repaso.texto: Escribe una frase de aviso amable: pedir a los vecinos que devuelvan las herramientas al cobertizo.
repaso.respuesta: We kindly ask neighbours to return the tools to the shed.
aceptadas: Please return the tools to the shed.
Neighbours are kindly asked to return the tools to the shed.
We ask neighbours to return the tools to the shed.
We kindly ask you to return the tools to the shed.
Please remember to return the tools to the shed.
repaso.feedback: We kindly ask… to + verbo convierte una orden formal en una petición cercana.
